title: AI Firewall: The Data Firewall for AI (2026 Guide)
summary: An AI firewall controls what reaches AI tools and agents. Strac is the data firewall for AI: it redacts and blocks PII, PHI, and secrets at the browser, endpoint, and MCP before they reach ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or any AI agent.
body_markdown:
**Short answer:** An AI firewall is a security control between AI and your data that decides what is allowed. Strac is the **data firewall for AI** : it sits at the AI boundary, in the[browser extension](https://www.strac.io/integration/browser-dlp) , the[endpoint agent](https://www.strac.io/endpoint-dlp) , and across[MCP DLP](https://www.strac.io/blog/mcp-dlp) , and redacts or blocks sensitive data like PII, PHI, card numbers, and secrets before it ever reaches ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, or any AI agent.


The data firewall for AI: sensitive data is caught before it reaches the model.


## ✨ What is an AI firewall?


An AI firewall sits between AI and your data and decides what is allowed through.


An AI firewall is the control layer that sits between AI tools or agents and the people and data they touch, and decides what is allowed through. As teams adopt ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, and autonomous agents, an AI firewall is how security teams keep sensitive data and risky actions under control without blocking AI outright.


## ✨ The two kinds of AI firewall: network vs data


The term covers two different controls, and most organizations need both:


Type What it protects against Examples


Network / prompt firewall for AI Prompt injection, jailbreaks, abusive traffic, malicious output Network-security vendors


Data firewall for AI Sensitive data (PII, PHI, PCI, secrets) flowing into or out of AI Strac


A network firewall for AI watches the traffic for attacks. A **data firewall** watches the data, and stops regulated or confidential data from reaching the model in the first place. They solve different problems, so running both is common.


Strac redacts sensitive data at the boundary, before the model ever sees it.

One data firewall for AI across the browser, the endpoint, and MCP agents.

- **On the endpoint.** The[endpoint agent](https://www.strac.io/endpoint-dlp) covers desktop AI apps (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT desktop) with block, warn, allow, and audit modes, including screenshots via OCR.

The data firewall in action: Strac blocks a sensitive upload to an AI tool, live.


## ✨ Control what each AI agent can access


A firewall is also about access, not just content. Strac gives each AI agent only the data its task needs: it governs what an agent can reach over MCP, redacts sensitive values in every tool response, and lets you cut an agent’s access in one step. That is agent access control and data loss prevention in one layer. See[MCP gateway](https://www.strac.io/blog/mcp-gateway) and[agentic AI security](https://www.strac.io/blog/agentic-ai-security) .


Govern access per agent and per tool: allow, block, or redact.


## ✨ What the AI firewall catches


Strac ships 100+ detectors and finds sensitive data even inside images, screenshots, and documents using OCR and ML:


Strac flags the SSN, card, and email in an AI prompt and blocks before send.


- **PII** : SSNs, passports, driver’s licenses, dates of birth, addresses.
- **PHI** : medical records, ICD-10 codes, prescription data.
- **PCI** : credit card numbers, bank accounts, routing numbers.
- **Secrets and code** : API keys, credentials, and proprietary source code.
- **Custom** : any pattern you describe in plain English.


## ✨ Catch the shadow AI your firewall does not know about


Strac surfaces shadow AI, so the firewall covers the AI you did not know about.


An AI firewall only works on the AI you know about. Strac surfaces[shadow AI](https://www.strac.io/blog/shadow-ai) , the unsanctioned AI tools employees adopted, so the data firewall covers the whole AI surface, not just approved tools.


## ✨ Why you need an AI firewall now


AI adoption moved faster than the controls around it. Employees paste customer records into ChatGPT, developers drop source code into Claude, and autonomous agents pull data from your systems over MCP, all in channels traditional DLP never watched. The risk is specific:


One prompt can leak regulated data; the firewall catches it before it reaches the model.


- **Data retention.** Sensitive data sent to a model may be logged, cached, or used for training, outside your control.
- **One prompt, one leak.** A single paste can exfiltrate regulated data in seconds, with no file transfer to catch.
- **Agents at machine speed.** An over-permissioned agent can move data across systems faster than a human reviewer can react.
- **Shadow AI.** Teams adopt tools security never approved, so the leak happens where no one is looking.


An AI firewall closes these gaps by controlling the data at the AI boundary, so your team keeps using AI without sending regulated data to someone else’s model.

## How to choose an AI firewall


Not all AI firewalls do the same job. Use this checklist:


- **Data or network?** Decide whether you need attack filtering (network/prompt firewall), data protection (data firewall), or both.
- **Coverage.** Does it cover every AI tool across the browser, endpoint, and MCP, or just one approved model?
- **Remediation.** Can it redact, block, warn, and allow, or only alert?
- **Detection depth.** 100+ data types, custom detectors, and OCR for images and screenshots.
- **Agents.** Does it govern what AI agents can access over MCP?
- **Shadow AI.** Does it discover unsanctioned AI tools?
- **Audit.** A full, exportable trail mapped to HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, and GDPR.

## 🌶️ Spicy FAQs: AI firewall


### How do I stop sensitive data from going into an AI model?


Put a data control at the point where data enters AI: the browser, the endpoint, and the MCP connection to AI agents. Strac inspects what a person or agent sends and redacts or blocks PII, PHI, card numbers, and secrets before it reaches the model, so the sensitive data never leaves your environment and the model never sees it. Your team keeps using AI; only the sensitive values are removed.


### How do I keep sensitive data out of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude?


Use a data firewall for AI that covers every tool. Strac works in the browser (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity), on the desktop (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT desktop), and across MCP for AI agents. It detects sensitive data in prompts, pastes, uploads, and screenshots, then redacts or blocks it before the AI receives it, with a full audit trail.


### Is an AI firewall the same as DLP?


An AI firewall is DLP applied at the AI boundary. Traditional DLP watched email, network, and files; an AI data firewall extends the same detect-and-redact logic to AI chat, pastes, uploads, screenshots, and agent tool calls, where data now actually leaks.


### Do I need an AI firewall if I already have a network firewall?


Usually yes. A network firewall for AI blocks attacks and abusive traffic but does not stop your own employees or agents from sending sensitive data to a model. A data firewall for AI does, so many teams run both.


### How fast can I deploy an AI firewall?


With Strac, most teams are enforcing across multiple AI tools within the first hour. There is no network re-architecture: you connect the browser extension, the endpoint agent, and MCP for agents, then set policy.


### What is an AI firewall?


An AI firewall is a security control that sits between AI tools or agents and the people and data interacting with them, and decides what is allowed. There are two kinds: a network or prompt firewall that filters prompts and model output for attacks and abuse, and a data firewall that stops sensitive data from flowing into or out of AI. Strac is the data firewall.


### What is a data firewall for AI?


A data firewall for AI inspects the data moving to and from AI tools and agents, and redacts, blocks, warns, or allows it by policy, so sensitive data like PII, PHI, card numbers, and secrets never reaches the model. Strac enforces this at the browser, the endpoint, and across MCP, so it covers every AI tool, not one approved model.


### What is the difference between an AI firewall and an LLM firewall?


They describe the same idea at different scopes. An LLM firewall is scoped to a large language model; an AI firewall is the broader term covering any AI tool, including agents and embedded AI features. A data firewall like Strac applies to both.


### Does an AI firewall stop data leaks?


A network or prompt firewall filters prompts and output for attacks, but does not stop your sensitive data from being sent to the model. Stopping data leaks requires a data firewall that inspects what is being sent. That is what Strac does: it redacts or blocks PII, PHI, and secrets before they leave your environment.


### How is Strac different from a network firewall for AI?


Network firewalls for AI (and prompt firewalls) focus on blocking attacks, prompt injection, and abusive traffic. Strac focuses on the data: it discovers and redacts sensitive data at the AI boundary across the browser, endpoint, and MCP, and governs what AI agents can access. Many teams run both, a network firewall for attacks and Strac for data.


### Does the AI firewall cover AI agents and MCP?


Yes. Strac sits in the MCP path between an AI agent and your tools as a reverse proxy, and redacts sensitive values in tool responses before the model sees them, agentlessly. See MCP DLP and MCP gateway.
